draft.title: One quantity as a percentage
card: To write one quantity as a percentage of another, write the part as a fraction of the whole. Divide the part by the whole.
Then multiply by 100 to turn the result into a percentage.
Both quantities must use the same units. Change one first if they do not, such as minutes and hours.
Example: 18 out of 24. \(18 \div 24 = 0.75\), and \(0.75 \times 100 = 75\), so the answer is 75%.
draft.remember: Part divided by whole, times 100, with matching units.

a.q: Sam scored 14 out of 20 on a quiz. What percentage is this?
a.why: \(14 \div 20 = 0.7\), and \(0.7 \times 100 = 70\), so the score is 70%. Writing 14% only uses the part and does not divide by the whole.
a.clue: Divide the part by the whole first.

b.q: Priya rides for 45 minutes of a 3 hour trip to Bendigo. What percentage of the trip is this?
b.why: Change 3 hours to 180 minutes. \(45 \div 180 = 0.25\), and \(0.25 \times 100 = 25\), so it is 25%. Using 45 and 3 together without matching units gives 15 and then 1500%, which is wrong.
b.clue: Put both times in minutes first.

problems.detail: The why describes the mismatched-units mistake as giving 1500%, which is not an option. The 15% option (45 ÷ 3 without multiplying by 100) goes unexplained, so the why does not match the distractor a student may have picked.

check.summary: Both answers are correct (70% and 25%), and the card is accurate. The only issue is minor: why (b) explains a 1500% error that is not an option and does not address the 15% distractor.

b.q: Priya rides for 45 minutes of a 3 hour trip to Bendigo. What percentage of the trip is this?
b.why: Change 3 hours to 180 minutes. \(45 \div 180 = 0.25\), and \(0.25 \times 100 = 25\), so it is 25%. The answer 15% comes from \(45 \div 3\), which mixes minutes with hours, and 75% uses only one hour, 60 minutes, as the whole.
b.clue: Put both times in minutes first.
